concepts.name: Hydrogen atom as a reduced particle
concepts.statement: The internal motion of the electron and proton about their center of mass is that of one particle of reduced mass μ at the position r of the electron relative to the proton; since the proton is so much heavier, the chapter takes μ as the electron mass and puts the proton at the center of mass.

concepts.name: Central potential
concepts.statement: A potential energy that depends only on the distance r from a center and on no angle, as the Coulomb attraction between the electron and the proton does.

concepts.name: Schrödinger equation of the hydrogen atom
concepts.statement: The time-independent Schrödinger equation of the hydrogen atom uses the kinetic energy operator of the rigid rotor in spherical coordinates, with r now free to vary, and the Coulomb potential energy −e²/4πε₀r of the electron and proton.

concepts.name: Square of the angular momentum operator
concepts.statement: The operator for the square of the angular momentum, the angular part of the Laplacian times −ħ²; the book writes it M̂² and, for an electron, L̂². It is also the sum of the squares of the three component operators.

concepts.name: Separating the radial and angular motion
concepts.statement: Because L̂² does not involve r, a product ψ = R(r)Y(θ, φ) separates the hydrogen atom's equation into a radial differential equation and an angular one, each equal to the same constant λ.

concepts.name: Eigenvalues of the square of the angular momentum
concepts.statement: The spherical harmonics are the eigenfunctions of L̂², with eigenvalue l(l + 1)ħ², the rigid rotor's J(J + 1)ħ² in the notation for electrons.

concepts.name: Radial equation of the hydrogen atom
concepts.statement: With λ = l(l + 1)ħ², the radial part of the hydrogen atom's equation is an equation for R(r) alone, in which the angular momentum enters as the term l(l + 1)ħ²/2μr² beside the potential energy.

concepts.name: Radial function
concepts.statement: The factor R(r) of a hydrogen atom wavefunction, a solution of the radial equation, which describes how far the electron is from the proton.

concepts.name: Hydrogen atom wavefunctions
concepts.statement: The solutions of the hydrogen atom's Schrödinger equation are products of a radial function and a spherical harmonic, labelled by three quantum numbers n, l and m_l; |ψ|² dτ is the probability of finding the electron in the volume element dτ at r, θ, φ.

concepts.name: Principal quantum number
concepts.statement: The quantum number n = 1, 2, 3, … of the hydrogen atom, which fixes its energy.

concepts.name: Angular momentum quantum number
concepts.statement: The quantum number l of the hydrogen atom, which fixes the magnitude of the electron's angular momentum; it is also called the azimuthal or orbital quantum number.

concepts.name: Magnetic quantum number
concepts.statement: The quantum number m_l of the hydrogen atom, which fixes the z component of the angular momentum; it is named for the dependence of the energy on m_l in a magnetic field.

concepts.name: Allowed values of n, l and m_l
concepts.statement: The boundary conditions allow n = 1, 2, 3, …; l = 0 to n − 1; and 2l + 1 values of m_l from −l to +l in integer steps.

concepts.name: Degeneracy of the hydrogen levels
concepts.statement: The number of orbitals with a given n, all of one energy, is n².

concepts.name: Orbital letters s, p, d, f
concepts.statement: The letters that code the value of l: s for 0, p for 1, d for 2, f for 3, then alphabetically from g; they come from early spectroscopy (sharp, principal, diffuse, fundamental).

concepts.name: Atomic orbital
concepts.statement: A function that describes one electron in an atom; the hydrogen atom wavefunctions are its atomic orbitals, and an electron described by one is said to be in it. An orbital is not an orbit: it gives no trajectory.

concepts.name: Real orbitals from complex ones
concepts.statement: Since any combination of degenerate solutions is a solution, the complex wavefunctions with m_l = ±1 (and ±2) can be combined into real ones such as p_x and p_y; only m_l = 0 belongs to one real orbital (p_z, d_z²) by itself.

concepts.name: Picturing an orbital
concepts.statement: An orbital's density is a function of three variables, pictured by shading small volume elements in proportion to ψ*ψ, by contour maps in a plane, or by plotting the radial and angular parts separately.

concepts.name: Radial node
concepts.statement: A value of r, other than 0 or ∞, at which the radial function is zero.

concepts.name: Number of radial nodes
concepts.statement: A hydrogen wavefunction has n − l − 1 radial nodes: none for 1s, one for 2s, and so on; the roots of its Laguerre polynomial are its radial nodes.

concepts.name: Only s orbitals are nonzero at the nucleus
concepts.statement: Every s function has a nonzero value at r = 0, while p, d, f and all other functions go to zero at the origin.

concepts.name: Radial probability density
concepts.statement: The square R(r)*R(r) of the radial function, the density of the electron at a point a distance r from the proton.

concepts.name: Radial distribution function
concepts.statement: The probability density of finding the electron anywhere on the sphere of radius r: the density on that sphere times its area 4πr², which for a normalized radial function is r²R(r)² (the book writes 4πr²R*R, which counts the 4π twice). It is zero at r = 0, rises with the r² term and falls once the exponential decay wins.

concepts.name: Orbital angular momentum
concepts.statement: The angular momentum of a particle about the origin, the cross product of its position and its momentum, with components L_x, L_y and L_z; for a circular orbit its magnitude is mvr.

concepts.name: Operators for the components of angular momentum
concepts.statement: The operators L̂_x, L̂_y and L̂_z, written from the classical components with the position and momentum operators; in spherical coordinates L̂_z = −iħ ∂/∂φ.

concepts.name: Magnitude of the angular momentum
concepts.statement: The square of the angular momentum can take only the values l(l + 1)ħ², so its magnitude is √(l(l + 1)) ħ, with l = 0, 1, 2, …; a state of quantum number l is often said to have angular momentum l for short.

concepts.name: Quantized z component of angular momentum
concepts.statement: The z component of the angular momentum can take only the values m_l ħ, with m_l an integer from −l to l.

concepts.name: Commutation relations of angular momentum
concepts.statement: The components of orbital angular momentum do not commute: [L̂_x, L̂_y] = iħL̂_z and its cyclic permutations. Any three operators that satisfy these relations represent the components of some sort of angular momentum.

concepts.name: Vector model of angular momentum
concepts.statement: A state with quantum numbers l and m_l is drawn as a vector of length √(l(l + 1)) ħ whose z component is m_l ħ; since L_x and L_y cannot be known with L_z, every such vector, on a cone about z, represents it equally.

concepts.name: Radial function far from the nucleus
concepts.statement: Far from the nucleus the radial function decays as an exponential in r/na₀, like the harmonic oscillator's Gaussian tail but with r in place of r².

concepts.name: Associated Laguerre polynomials
concepts.statement: The polynomials L_{n,l}(r), from the truncated power series of the radial equation, labelled by n and l; acceptable solutions need n ≥ l + 1.

concepts.name: Hydrogen radial functions
concepts.statement: The radial functions are products of a normalization constant, (r/a₀)^l, an associated Laguerre polynomial and the decaying exponential, which overpowers the polynomial so that R(r) goes to zero at large r. With the nuclear charge Z they serve every one-electron atom or ion.

concepts.name: Energy levels of the hydrogen atom
concepts.statement: The condition n ≥ l + 1 quantizes the energy, giving the same levels as the Bohr model: E_n = −μe⁴/8ε₀²h²n², which depend on n alone.

concepts.name: Bohr and Schrödinger models compared
concepts.statement: The Schrödinger model gives no orbits, only probabilities; its angular momentum is √(l(l + 1)) ħ, which can be zero, where Bohr's is a whole number of ħ; and its quantum numbers arise from solving the equation, where Bohr postulated them.

concepts.name: Electron density distribution
concepts.statement: The probability distribution P_n of an electron in a definite energy level, read as the fraction of its charge in each small volume of space; it is measured in electronic charges per unit volume, e⁻/a₀³ in atomic units.

concepts.name: s orbitals are spherically symmetric
concepts.statement: For every n one orbital, the s orbital, is independent of direction: its density depends on r alone, so its contours in a plane through the nucleus are circles; the other n² − 1 are concentrated in planes or along axes.

concepts.name: Volume of a thin spherical shell
concepts.statement: The volume between spheres of radius r and r + Δr is 4πr²Δr when Δr is small, since the terms in Δr² and Δr³ become negligible.

concepts.name: Most probable radius of the 1s electron
concepts.statement: The radial distribution function of the hydrogen ground state is zero at the nucleus, rises to a maximum at r_max = a₀ and falls off; since the curve is unsymmetrical, the average r̄ lies beyond r_max.

concepts.name: Torque
concepts.statement: What changes a system's angular momentum, as a force changes its linear momentum.

concepts.name: A central force leaves angular momentum constant
concepts.statement: A force directed along r, like the attraction of the nucleus, changes only the electron's linear momentum: it exerts no torque, so the angular momentum of the orbit stays constant.

concepts.name: Conserved quantities are quantized
concepts.statement: The book's rule of thumb: any quantity that is constant in a classical system is conserved and quantized in the quantum system, so an undisturbed atom has quantized energy and angular momentum.

concepts.name: s orbitals carry no angular momentum
concepts.statement: When l = 0 the angular momentum is zero; only such s electrons have spherical density distributions and place density at the nucleus.

concepts.name: Number of nodes
concepts.statement: The number of nodes of a hydrogen orbital grows with its energy and equals n − 1, while the average r grows with n.

concepts.name: Shape of a p orbital
concepts.statement: A p orbital (l = 1) is concentrated along an axis: positive on one side of the nodal plane through the nucleus and negative on the other, with two lobes of circular cross section and no density at the nucleus.

concepts.name: Shape of a d orbital
concepts.statement: A d orbital (l = 2) has two angular nodes and no density at the nucleus; only d_z² belongs to one value of m_l (0), the others being combinations.

concepts.name: Zeeman effect
concepts.statement: The shift of an orbital's energy in an external magnetic field, which depends on m_l; with no field the 2l + 1 values of m_l have the same energy.

concepts.name: Electron–electron repulsion
concepts.statement: The Coulomb potential energy e²/4πε₀r_ij of two electrons a distance r_ij apart, positive because like charges repel.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian of a multi-electron atom
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian of an atom with nuclear charge Z and n electrons, nucleus fixed at the center of mass, has a kinetic energy term and an attraction to the nucleus for each electron, and a repulsion term for each pair of electrons.

concepts.name: Multi-electron atoms cannot be solved exactly
concepts.statement: The repulsion terms in 1/r_ij depend on two electrons' coordinates at once, so the Hamiltonian does not separate electron by electron and the Schrödinger equation has no exact solution even for helium.

concepts.name: Multi-electron wavefunction
concepts.statement: A single function of the coordinates of all the electrons at once, whose square gives the probability of finding the electrons, though not particular ones, in a region.

concepts.name: Orbital approximation
concepts.statement: Writing a multi-electron wavefunction as a product of one-electron functions, the orbitals, so that the energy is approximately the sum of the one-electron energies.
